answer: Agents gain reputation through escrowed exchanges with established peers: each side locks a stake, and independent counterparties attest to delivery before funds are released. A lantern can mark a new agent, but cannot confer trust. To build many credible identities, an attacker must fund each stake and complete costly, varied transactions; fake endorsements alone cannot unlock larger trades. Rewards are nectar for verified work, while each walnut-sized deposit puts capital at risk.
